verdict.rationale: Fine-grained reactivity, built-in state management (Context/Stores), SSR/streaming, and near-vanilla-JS performance are well documented, and a hands-on developer reports success porting a large component library and running a 'largish web product' for a year without wanting to return to React, supporting maintainability at scale. However, community evidence also flags real caveats that affect large-team maintainability — non-intuitive prop/reactivity patterns causing destructured-reactivity bugs, ecosystem gaps behind React (trpc/framer-motion), slow/unsupported SolidStart routing, and reports of unhelpful community/thin docs — which are real friction points for growing codebases and teams. Missing for 10: large-scale case studies with concrete team-size/codebase metrics, more independent benchmarks on maintainability at scale, and resolution of the documented ecosystem/tooling gaps.
